symptom: `describe page` renders a pluggable widget with two configured datasources as if it had one, so describe -> exec drops the second binding
cause: The describer had one slot (rawWidget.DataSource) and every emitter branch read it directly. Worse, the per-widget extractors each know about ONE of their widget's datasources — the drop-down filter's reads `refOptions` and never `linkedDs` — and they run BEFORE the generic fallback, whose `if widget.DataSource == nil` guard then skipped it entirely
insight: Whether a widget is multi-source is a property of the STORED DOCUMENT, not of which per-widget extractor happened to run — so the detection must run unconditionally, after them. Route every emitter branch through one helper (`appendWidgetDataSources`) or a branch will keep describing multi-source widgets as single-source; there were 7 call sites reading w.DataSource. Adding a new condition to the generic pluggable branch made it STEAL widgets from the filter branch further down and silently drop CaptionAttribute — branch order in the emitter is load-bearing, so widen the existing branch's gate instead. An unresolvable schema key must fall back to the unnamed spelling, never be skipped: skipping is #956's silent drop by another route. The empty-reference filter does double duty — an unset second datasource drops out, so single-source output stays byte-identical
